page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Motion in a Straight Line · 2 marks

steps.label: Uniform motion
lines: In uniform motion a body covers equal
distances in equal intervals of time,
Its x–t graph is a straight line.
steps.why: The phrase "however small the interval" is what rules out a body that averages the same speed while speeding up and slowing down within each interval.
common_mistakes: Leaving out "equal intervals of time", which is what makes the definition precise.

recall.must_convey: That in uniform motion equal distances are covered in equal intervals of time and the position time graph is a straight line.

steps.memory_tip: Uniform is about equal distances in equal TIMES, not about a straight path.
steps.margin_note: The words "however small" are worth including.

steps.why: A curved position–time graph means the slope is changing, and the slope is the velocity, so a curve is the signature of acceleration.
common_mistakes: Saying non-uniform motion means the body moves along a curved path. The path and the graph are different things.

recall.must_convey: That non-uniform motion covers unequal distances in equal times, has a curved position time graph and has acceleration.

steps.memory_tip: Curved x–t graph means changing slope, and slope is velocity — so there is acceleration.

insider_note: Equal distances in equal intervals is the phrase the examiner wants. Give the graph shape for each.
